facts.content: A 45-year-old female has a 1-day history of shortness of breath.
The patient has right-sided back pain on deep breath for 1 day.
facts.source_text: 45F with 1-day history of SOB, right-sided back pain on deep breath

facts.content: The patient reports a slight fever without a measured temperature.
The patient has a cough with hemoptysis occurring twice.
The patient has a 2-week history of fatigue.
The patient reports decreased exercise tolerance for 2 weeks.
facts.source_text: 2-week history of fatigue, decreased exercise tolerance

facts.content: The patient reports a sensation of palpitations for 2 weeks.
facts.source_text: 2-week history of fatigue, decreased exercise tolerance, palpitations sensation

facts.content: The patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus.
The patient is taking methotrexate for SLE.
The last dose of methotrexate was taken this morning.
The patient has no known allergies.
The patient does not smoke.
The patient lives alone in a flat.
The patient works an office desk job.
The patient has a cat at home.
The patient reports a self-measured pulse of approximately 66 to 74 beats per minute.
Good peripheral capillary refill was visualized via camera.
facts.source_text: Good peripheral capillary refill visualized via camera

facts.content: Throat inspection revealed no abnormalities.
No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy was reported.
There is an acute chest infection versus pneumonia in a patient with shortness of breath, pleuritic pain, fever, and hemoptysis on immunosuppressant therapy.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute chest infection vs pneumonia - presenting with SOB, pleuritic pain, fever, hemoptysis in patient on immunosuppressant

facts.content: The patient has SLE on methotrexate with consideration of increased infection risk.
facts.source_text: 2. SLE on methotrexate - consider infection risk

facts.content: Pulmonary embolism or malignancy is to be ruled out but considered less likely given the acute presentation and absence of risk factors per history.
facts.source_text: 3. Rule out pulmonary embolism or malignancy - less likely given acute presentation and absence of risk factors per history

facts.content: An urgent face-to-face clinical review today is planned for chest auscultation, vital signs including blood pressure, pulse, and temperature, and a full physical examination.
facts.source_text: Urgent face-to-face clinical review today for chest auscultation, vital signs (BP, pulse, temp), and full physical exam

facts.content: A chest X-ray may be performed after assessment depending on clinical findings.
facts.source_text: Possible chest X-ray post-assessment depending on clinical findings

facts.content: Antibiotics will be considered if an infection is confirmed.
The patient was advised to contact the support team to arrange a clinic appointment.
facts.source_text: Patient advised to contact support team to arrange clinic appointment

facts.content: The patient was counselled about the currently low likelihood of lung cancer and the need for close follow-up.
